# Spelling word bank and generated items

*Candidate content: generated by rule from openly licensed lexical data, not reviewed by educators.
Difficulty is a feature-based estimate, not calibrated.*

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `wordbank.json` | 818 words, each with its spelling pattern (capability and ladder step), base word and ending, accepted variant spellings, rule-made misspellings with the misconception each shows, and for some words a short meaning and an example sentence. Every field names its source. |
| `generated-items.json` | 2,348 items made from the word bank by five templates: add the ending, hear and spell, choose the spelling, meaning and first letter, homophone in context. |
| `retired-generated.json` | Earlier versions of generated items whose content has changed (empty so far), so old answers are still scored as answered. |
| `blocklist.txt` | Words kept out of the bank, its meanings and its sentences (ages 10–15). |
| `exclusions.txt` | Words kept out after a first review of a sample: too rare or specialised for the age group. |
| `licences/` | The sources' licence and copyright notices, verbatim. |

## Sources and attribution

| Source | Version used | Licence | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **English Speller Database (ESDB, formerly SCOWL)**, Kevin Atkinson and contributors, [github.com/en-wl/wordlist](https://github.com/en-wl/wordlist) | commit `1e5b7d3a` | MIT-like; notices in `licences/SCOWL-Copyright.txt`, kept verbatim, including the UKACD and WordNet notices | Which words exist (the size-35 list), British spelling with American and -ize spellings as accepted variants, part of speech, inflected forms, and a commonness signal (its `[ukfreq]` tag, from Brian Kelk's public-domain UK frequency list) |
| **The CMU Pronouncing Dictionary**, Carnegie Mellon University, [github.com/cmusphinx/cmudict](https://github.com/cmusphinx/cmudict) | commit `74790861` | BSD 2-clause, `licences/CMUdict-LICENSE.txt` | Syllables and stress (for doubling rules), homophone groups, and which words must never be dictated because they sound like another word |
| **Open English WordNet**, the Open English Wordnet team, derived from Princeton WordNet, [github.com/globalwordnet/english-wordnet](https://github.com/globalwordnet/english-wordnet) | commit `bff3181f` (2025 development line) | CC BY 4.0, `licences/OEWN-LICENSE.md`; Princeton WordNet licence, `licences/WordNet-LICENSE.txt` | Short meanings (clues), example sentences (homophones), and the relations that confirm a prefix or suffix really joins its base |

**Changes made to the sources.** Words were selected and filtered by rule (and by the two lists above).
Meanings and example sentences are used as they appear in Open English WordNet, except that the
target word is replaced by a blank in homophone items. Patterns, misspellings and difficulty estimates
are OpenPath's own, made by rule. Pronunciations are not shipped.

**Not used** (decision 4 of 12 October 2026): wordfreq and Tatoeba, pending a licence review.

## Rebuilding

The pipeline downloads nothing. Check out each source at the pinned commit (the script refuses any
other), build SCOWL's database with `make` in its checkout, then:

```
python3 tools/english/spelling/build_wordbank.py --scowl <wordlist> --cmudict <cmudict> --oewn <english-wordnet>
node tools/english/spelling/generate.ts
```

`node tools/english/spelling/generate.ts --check` (run in CI) fails if the committed items differ from a
fresh generation. An item whose content changes gets a new version; the old one moves to
`retired-generated.json`.

## How generated items are used

- They target only the three spelling capabilities of framework 0.2.0 (inflections, homophones,
  morphological), on the existing difficulty ladders. There is no separate spelling score.
- They are never used for placement.
- **Until a person has checked an item** (`generated.checked`), an answer to it is kept in the learner's
  ledger as practice but changes no estimate (`updater.ts`). The spelling module's own word memory
  and pattern accuracy use these answers; capability estimates come only from hand-written items.
